steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix together corn syrup, sugar, melted butter, and salt in a large bowl. Add eggs and beat until well combined. Pour mixture into the pie crust and sprinkle pecans over top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 50 to 60 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let cool to room temperature before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Kentucky Pecan Pie
raw_recipe.description: Corn syrup and brown sugar do magical things in this simple pecan pie with a rich, gooey, and delicious filling. Perfect for holiday bake sales.
raw_recipe.name: Kentucky Pecan Pie

review.reviewBody: This recipe was awesome. It is the best pecan pie I have ever eaten. Although, I did add 1 teaspoon of vanilla to the recipe. That gave it excellent flavor. I made this pie for Christmas dinner, everyone raved about how wonderful it was. Even people who didn't care for pecan pie said that it was excellent. I would recommend this recipe to anyone.

This recipe needs 3/4 tsp vanilla, with it his is the best pecan pie. I get rave reviews. Well except for my mother in law. She insisted I use her traditional recipe because hers was better. Funny thing, one year I made both and she loved her recipe but my pie was gone in a flash. There is nothing wrong with the recipe. I have made this for years.*****Don't forget the salt. The trick to balance the sweet is more pecans and how you put the pie together. Put a nice layer of chopped pecans on the bottom before filling, some will rise and become candied on the top. Then put a nice layer of chopped on the top and then decorate with whole. I don't use a lot of whole because it makes it messier to cut up and eat.**** If your pie is too high in the oven it will take longer to set up. Ive always used a glass pan. You have to use a ring to protect the crust. I know at higher altitudes Ive had to put foil over the whole pie for an additional 10 minutes to get it to set. I give it a poke with a toothpick and a wiggle if it jiggles it needs more time. Experienced cooks know cooking times can be approximate. Let it cool completely on the counter to set. I always make mine the night before.******* For deep dish pies add 1/4 more sugar and syrup, one more egg and adjust to 1 tsp vanilla and 1/4 tsp salt.

I did make a couple of changes. I doubled the recipe, added 1 extra egg and 1/2 cup of molasses. Before adding the eggs I beat them till they were mixed well and then strained them through a sieve. I then added the eggs to the rest of the ingredients. I also added an extra 1/2 cup of pecans.
I made 2 crust.
2-1/2 cups King Arthur Flour, 2 sticks (very cold) unsalted butter cubed, 1/2 tsp salt. I put the above 3 ingredients in a food processor and pulsed for about 30 to 45 seconds
I added about 7 tablespoons of ice water.
Mix till all ingredients hold together. Form a ball and cut in half. Roll out (both if making 2 pies ) place in pie pans ( I used 10 inch). Put in frig till pie mix is ready and bake at 350° about 1 hr to 1 hr 10 min.
I thought this pie would be extremely sweet but to my surprise it was just right.

I toasted my pecans in a dry pan for 5-10 min.... . Used good Irish Butter and added some vanilla to the mix... I also followed another reviewer, and placed 1/2 of the pecans on the bottom of the pie shell and mixed the rest in the syrup mix. This pie is decadent !

I paired this with your No Fail Pie Crust 1 and am now the official Thanksgiving pie baker! I added the vanilla as suggested, but I also altered the baking directions. I started by baking the pie at 425* for the first 15 minutes, then reduced the heat to 350* for the remaining time. I also baked it on a parchment lined baking sheet on the BOTTOM rack. My crust browned beautifully and was flakey on the bottom and the side. Voted best pecan pie in my family!

I agree that no changes need to be made to make this simple, yet fabulous pie.
I did enhance it with 1tsp.vanilla, and 1 Tbl Boubon. For extra excitement I added 1/4 c of chocolate chips in the bottom of the pie crust, mostly for the kids. Also used 2 cups Peacans and toasted them for 7 min on parchment paper. Simple or dressed up, really good!!

Loved this!!! Easy peezy to make but I put mine in a pecan crumb crust which was the hit it always is in my cheesecake.
Ingredients
3/4 cup all-purpose flour
1/4 cup sugar

Directions

In a bowl, combine the flour, sugar, pecans and lemon peel, cut in butter until crumbly. Combine egg yolk and vanilla; stir into flour mixture. Press onto the bottom of a greased 10-in. springform pan. Bake at 400 degrees F for 8-11 minutes or until edges are lightly browned. Cool on a wire rack. 

1/4 cup finely chopped pecans
1 teaspoon grated lemon peel
6 tablespoons cold butter (no substitutes)
1 egg yolk
1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract

Easy & excellent! Have made several times over the holidays & it’s been a huge hit (w changes due to other reviewers, so 4 stars for this recipe, 5 stars w changes). Added 1tsp vanilla & an extra 1/2c pecans (1.5c total), & reduced brown sugar to 3/4c.
I added a teaspoon of vanilla extract and a tablespoon of Kentucky bourbon to the mixture and it was so good.

Excellent recipe. I used dark corn syrup and added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon to the mix. I also doubled the pecans, using whole ones for the top layer.
The crust I use has four ingredients: AP flour, lard, salt, and ice water.

This was my jumping off recipe for a chocolate pecan pie. I'm basing my review for my additions. However, I can't imagine that it wouldn't be grand as it is written. I sprinkled the bottom of the deep dish crust, (unbaked), with semi-sweet chocolate chips. Instead of a full cup of light corn syrup I used 1/2 cup of light corn syrup and 1/2 cup of Lyle's Golden Cane Syrup, and added 2 tsp. of vanilla. It gave the pie a wonderful caramel taste. I did have to bake about 1 1/2, but I tented the pie with aluminum foil so the top wouldn't burn. It was absolutely what I was looking for, and it will be my go-to recipe in the future. Thanks for letting me experiment with your wonderful recipe, Laurie.
Love it, my favorite! I use dark brown sugar (when I can find it!) and 4 large eggs, because the eggs these days are not as large as they used to be.
I substituted pecans for pecan flour bc I don't have back teeth but love this pie to death literally. It's amazing 😻

Love this recipe. The ONLY thing I do differently is pouring the pecans into the pie mix before I pour the mix into the shell. During cooking they will fight their way to the top and when they get there, they will be candy coated. I never worry about making sure they are evenly distributed. The oven always figures it out.

I’m 65 years old and have made many, many pecan pie recipes over the years. This recipe is hands down the BEST. People who said it’s too sweet need to make a fruit pie. Pecan pie is supposed to be sweet. This is recipe is perfect.
Great and easy recipe, I make it several times a year. Everyone loves it.

I am so happy I tried this recipe! It was my first attempt at a "regular" pecan pie. I have previously made them with bourbon and with chocolate, which were good. However, this KY Pecan Pie was not nearly as sweet as the others I made previously. I like that it allowed the flavor of the crust to come through and compliment the pecan filling. I will absolutely make this again!
I made this pie exactly as written. Pecan pie is always sweet, as was this one. Overall, it was good, but lacked something in the body of the pie. I will try another recipe next time.

Unfortunately, my pie never set. It looked perfect on top and because I followed the directions meticulously, I was very surprised when I cut into it to see a crisp top and a soupy, syrupy mess at the bottom. It seemed like too few pecans as well. I was hopeful for this recipe but it did not work for me, so I will try something else the next time around.
This is a recipe that I have been using for over 30 years. I do add a teaspoon of vanilla for that special flavour. As far as it been being too sweet, it is a pecan pie!
